data.current_description:
Reputation and bot probability for a browser fingerprint produced by https://www.layercall.com/fp.js.

This is the signal that survives an attacker rotating IPs and email addresses: a new VPN exit and a fresh disposable inbox are free, a new machine is not. The `device_id` is hashed in the browser and again before storage, so the stored value cannot be reversed to a device.

POST rather than GET because a device id in a query string ends up in access logs and Referer headers.
data.description_suggestion: Scores device reputation and bot probability for a browser fingerprint generated by LayerCall's fp.js library. Returns a 0-100 risk score and verdict indicating device trustworthiness and bot likelihood. Device fingerprints persist across IP and email changes, making them valuable for detecting repeat offenders. The device_id is hashed client-side and server-side for privacy—stored hashes cannot be reversed to identify the device. Use POST (not GET) to prevent device_id exposure in access logs and Referer headers.
